chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abū Usāmah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about vomiting: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: No.

key_terms.الْقَيْءِ: vomiting, the act being asked about in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for certain acts of worship
key_terms.لَا: no; the Imam’s ruling that it does not invalidate wudu
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: invalidates or breaks, in the legal sense

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting invalidate wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that vomiting does not invalidate wudu (ablution). It is a concise jurisprudential ruling related to ritual purity and acts of worship.
